gen-tourney-gf-preahvihear: Wide-tracked, athletic lettering with a flat, unvarying line weight. Tourney leads, then Preahvihear takes over with open letter mouths and a lofty x-height that lets paragraphs glide along.
gen-tourney-gf-sintony: Bulky, wide-tracked letters, every curve and straight cut to match. What stands out most is Sintony, whose chunky, tall midzone keeps every curve smooth and unclogged beneath Tourney.
gen-dafont-klill-switzer: Klill holds its curve endings well apart, big-bodied and unshaded. Switzer shares that tubular, wire-like build and its tall waist line, so the two sit together like one family.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-readex-pro: Bold, expressive letters held open rather than curled shut, with short ascenders. Readex Pro settles in behind it, with broad terminal gaps and a weight that never wavers from word to word.
gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-sofia-sans-semi-conde: Wallpoet lifts its lowercase high, with paper showing between letters. Sofia Sans Semi Condensed then carries the text at a constant weight, each curve entered through a big visible opening, so paragraphs move smoothly.
gen-megrim-gf-sulphur-point: Angular and futuristic, with a c as open as a bent paperclip. Sulphur Point backs it with a steady, marker-like line and bulky lowercase proportions, a sturdy partner for Megrim.
gen-fs-oswald-fs-quicksand: Tightly knit rows of confident, strong lettering. Oswald packs lines in with authority, while Quicksand keeps its bar thickness uniform and ends its terminals well away from the stem.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-akatab: Tightly packed rows, confident and strong. Akatab keeps its round letters cupped, not clenched, though Oswald shrunk to a small heading would lose some of its strong presence.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-noto-sans-nko: Strong, confident lettering that packs its rows tight. Noto Sans NKo then keeps a modern, contemporary tone, its see-through c openings letting paragraphs run light on the eye.
